newsitem.title: USA: IMF's Camdessus sees wage pressures in Venezuela.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Camdessus sees wage pressures in Venezuela.

text.p: International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus on Thursday said Venezuela's stabilization program was working well but warned that he saw excessive wage pressures building.
Camdessus told a news conference that the "Agenda Venezuela" program seemed to be an undeniable success.

"Confidence has reappeared, inflation has declined -- although not enough -- privatizations have started again, the banking system has strengthened and many distortions which paralyzed the economy have been eliminated," he said.
Venezuela's political parties have also reached agreement on reforming the social security system and the severance payment policy for the public sector, he noted.
"All this is significant but I also see that there is a disorderly and excessive wage pressure in view of the country's capacity and that creates difficulties in implementing the program," he added.
The Venezuelan government, which wants to extend its current IMF standby program, last month granted public servants a 75 percent wage increase.
Camdessus said that, nevertheless, the IMF was prepared to continue supporting Venezuela.

"Venezuela has much to do in strengthening its economy and its institutions. In Venezuela, as in many other countries, there are major institutional problems to be resolved after many years of paternalism, of populism ..." he said.
"Institutions have been discredited and the (Venezuelan) government is making every effort to reconstruct them and we are here to help," he added.
Last year Venezuela's inflation reached 100 percent. The IMF projects it as dropping to about 47 percent this year.
